name: Sundance Provincial Park - Emerson Lakes Campground
note: Alberta Parks campground in Sundance PP, ~56 km NE of Hinton via gravel Emerson Creek Road; 15 unserviced drive-in sites plus a group area on the Emerson Lakes chain, boat launch, vault toilets, free firewood, no potable water/hookups (generators OK). 7 sites reservable by phone, 8 FCFS; open May–Oct. --Claude

name: Fickle Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA campground on Fickle Lake, 31 km SW of Edson off Hwy 47; 36 drive-in sites for tents/RVs, some lakeside, boat launch, dock, pump water, vault toilets, fish-cleaning station, no hookups. Reservable by phone plus FCFS; open early May–Oct. --Claude

name: Freeman River Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small Alberta Parks PRA campground on the Freeman River, ~16 km south of Swan Hills off Hwy 32; 10 unserviced drive-in sites for tents/RVs among tall trees, fire pits, vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served ($20/night); open ~Jun–Oct. Adjacent OHV trails. --Claude

name: Cold Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park on the south shore of Cold Lake. 115 sites incl. power and power/water hookups plus walk-in tenting; showers, flush toilets, sewage disposal, boat launch, store, sandy beach. Open mid-May to early Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Moose Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park on Moose Lake, N of Bonnyville near Glendon. 59 drive-in sites, 47 with 15/30-amp power; picnic tables, firewood, toilets, sewage dump, boat launch, sandy beach. Open May-Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Whitney Lakes Provincial Park — Whitney Lake Campground
note: Whitney Lakes PP, Whitney Lake Campground: 53 sites (33 with 30-amp power), reservable via Alberta Parks; sandy beach, boat launch, showers. Many pull-in sites fit large rigs. Open mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Gregoire Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park on Gregoire Lake, ~30 km SE of Fort McMurray. 140 drive-in sites (80 unserviced, 60 powered) on the west shore, reservable (90-day window; season ~late June to mid-October); showers, laundry, dump station, campground store, beach, boat launch. --Claude

name: Hangingstone Provincial Recreation Area
note: Rustic Alberta Parks PRA campground 35 km south of Fort McMurray on Hwy 63, near the Hangingstone River. 59 unserviced drive-in sites (tents/RVs, trailers to ~35 ft) with firepits, picnic tables, hand-pump water, vault toilets, playground and picnic shelter. Reservable through Alberta Parks (ReserveAmerica ABPP, parkId 330336); ~$22/night, open mid-May to early Sep. --Claude

name: Granview Recreation Park
note: Community recreation park in the Town of Granum, run by the non-profit Granum Park Society; ~54 gravel sites, most full-service incl 25 pull-throughs (to 60 ft), plus par-3 golf, ball diamonds and a stocked pond; open May-Oct. Reservations by phone/Campspot. --Claude

name: Stavely Elks Pine Coulee Campground
note: Public campground on the west shore of Pine Coulee Reservoir (a provincial off-stream water-management reservoir); recreation held by the MD of Willow Creek and operated since 2021 by the non-profit Stavely Elks Lodge; ~25 RV/tent drive-in sites, powered ($35) and non-powered ($25), boat launch, dry toilets; open mid-Apr-Oct; FCFS plus reservable group areas. Not a members-only club park. --Claude

name: Fort Macleod Lions Club Campground
note: Lions Club-run municipal campground in John Zoeteman Park north of Fort Macleod on Hwy 811, along Willow Creek. ~30 unserviced (rustic) drive-in gravel-pad sites with fire pits/picnic tables, pit toilets, non-potable water; tent camping too. Open ~May-Sept. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Taber Municipal Park
note: Municipal District of Taber campground on the Oldman River, 4 km north of Taber on Hwy 864. 84 30-amp power sites (pull-through and back-in), showers/washrooms, sani-dump, potable water, free firewood; open ~May-Oct. Reservable online via Let's Camp (4 single-night sites held FCFS). --Claude

name: Irricana Municipal Campground (Founders Park)
note: Town of Irricana campground at Founders Park (1st St & 2nd Ave), across from Pioneer Acres Museum; 34 30-amp + two 50-amp powered sites, water, washrooms/showers, sani-dump, on-site community hall and trails; open May-Oct. Reservable online (Camp Reservations Canada, moving to Campspot). --Claude

name: Carstairs Municipal Campground
note: Town of Carstairs campground at Centre St & Hwy 2A; 28 sites with 15/30-amp power, water, tables, toilets, showers, sani-dump, playground and firewood; open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Village of Linden East Coulee Campground
note: Village of Linden's East Coulee Campground, in a coulee beside a stocked trout pond within the village; 7 gravel sites with water + 50-amp power, sani-dump nearby, open May-Oct. First-come, first-served with self-registration envelopes. --Claude

name: Tofield Campground
note: Town of Tofield municipal campground by the ball diamonds in town; 18 pull-through sites with 15/30-amp power (electric only), water, showers, coin dump, open May-Oct, self-registration. --Claude

name: Centennial Park Campground
note: Town of Rocky Mountain House municipal campground in the centre of town (across from Pioneer School); 15 treed sites - 5 with power/water, 10 non-serviced - showers, playground, open May-Sept long weekends. Reservations required online. --Claude

name: Beiseker Municipal Campground
note: Village of Beiseker municipal campground on the north edge of the village; 50 sites - 30 with water/power, 20 non-serviced - showers, camp kitchen, dump station, ball diamonds, open May-Oct. Reservable. --Claude

name: Village of Carbon Main Campground
note: Village of Carbon-operated town campground on Caradoc Ave near the pool/downtown; 22 serviced sites (30/50-amp, water, some sewer), flush toilets, free showers, camp kitchen. Open May long weekend to Thanksgiving; reservable online (Camp Reservations Canada). --Claude

name: Coal Lake South Park
note: Wetaskiwin County municipal campground at the south end of Coal Lake near the dam; ~14 serviced/unserviced sites, water, toilets, boat launch. Open mid-May to mid-Sept; reservable online (LetsCamp). --Claude

name: Cereal Campground
note: Community campground in the hamlet of Cereal (Special Areas No. 2) run by the Cereal & District Board of Trade; ~12-14 serviced lots with water and power, covered camp kitchen, outhouses, free sewer dump, easy pull-through access. Open ~May-Oct, ~$25/night, self-pay/first-come. --Claude

name: Grande Cache Municipal Campground
note: Municipal District of Greenview No. 16 campground in the hamlet of Grande Cache next to the golf course and ball diamonds; 77 sites (56 full-service, pull-through and back-in), fire pits, showers, washrooms, coin laundry. Open May long weekend to Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Hythe Municipal Campground
note: County of Grande Prairie No. 1 campground at Hythe, ~59 km W of Grande Prairie off Hwy 43; 24 sites with 15-30 amp power, tap water, dump station, showers/washrooms (in restored railway cabooses), free firewood. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Cold Lake M.D. Park
note: M.D. of Bonnyville campground on the shore of Cold Lake at 2301-1 Ave, short walk to Kinosoo Beach. 145 powered + 14 non-powered sites, ranging from lakefront to walk-up tent; potable water/RV fill, flush toilets, coin showers, laundry, onsite store, boat launch. Reservable online (letscamp.ca), open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Floatingstone Lake Campground
note: County of St. Paul campground on the south shore of Floatingstone Lake, ~4 km W and 8 km N of Ashmont. 46 powered (30 amp) + 19 non-powered sites in wooded loops; showers, dump station, free Wi-Fi, boat launch, fish-cleaning station, day-use picnic shelter, 24-hr attendant. Reservable online (letscamp.ca), open ~May long weekend-Labour Day. --Claude

name: Ethel Lake M.D. Park
note: Small M.D. of Bonnyville campground on Ethel Lake, ~3 min east of Kinosoo Beach area near Ardmore. 11 non-powered drive-in sites (self-contained RVs and tents); outhouses, hand pump (non-potable), boat launch, dock, swim area, picnic shelter, playground, fish-cleaning station. Reservable online (letscamp.ca), open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Calaway RV Park & Campground
note: Privately-run campground at Calaway Park amusement park west of Calgary off Trans-Canada Hwy 1. 100+ sites: 56 full-service, 41 partial (power), 7 unserviced/tent; pull-through and back-in, coin laundry, showers. Open weekends mid-May then daily early Jun-early Sep; reservable online or by phone. --Claude

name: Gold Springs Campground
note: Family campground run by the Gold Springs Park Society on a reservoir/oxbow of the Milk River, ~10 km north of the US border. ~70 sites, most with 30-amp power and water, pull-through options; also rental cabins (extra), showers, camp kitchens, playground, water slides, paddle boats, fishing and canoe access. Open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Devon Lions Campground
note: Lions-club community campground in the North Saskatchewan River valley at Devon, ~25 mi SW of Edmonton. About 230 powered gravel-pad sites; reservable; open May-Oct. 5 long pull-throughs; some mature trees make the biggest rigs tight but 23-ft rigs fit easily. --Claude

name: Willey West Campground
note: Campground in Eagle Point Provincial Park along the North Saskatchewan River ~6 km E of Drayton Valley off Hwy 22, operated by concessionaire Elevated Experience Camping; 90+ drive-in sites incl full-hookup (30-amp/water/sewer), power-only and unserviced plus pull-throughs for larger rigs; washrooms/showers, dump station, boat launch, trails and playground. Open ~May-Sept; reservable online. --Claude

name: Wetaskiwin Lions RV Campground
note: Lions Club-run community campground just east of town off Hwy 2A/13; ~27 fully-serviced sites, 22 power/water, 25 unserviced plus a tenting area, all 30-amp; showers, laundry, dump station, playground and a catch-and-release trout pond. Open May to late September; reservable by phone/website. --Claude

name: Pih-to-kwe Campground
note: Private campground in the trees off Hwy 22 just north of Drayton Valley; 41 sites with full-hookup and electric-only pull-throughs (15/30-amp), water, tables, grills, toilets and showers; camp kitchen and playground. Accepts big rigs. Open May-October, reservable online (LetsCamp). --Claude

name: Bannister Campground
note: Town of Provost campground on the north side of the recreation park beside the ball diamonds; 53 sites total — 45 with power/water/sewer (30-amp) and 8 tenting/campstove sites, shared shower house with Kinsmen Campground. Open May-October; register/pay at the Town office. --Claude

name: Blue Sky RV Park
note: Small private adult-oriented RV park in Clairmont, just north of Grande Prairie. 18 treed fully-serviced sites (water, 15/30-amp power, sewer, WiFi) with picnic tables, patios and fire pits; flush toilets, showers, coin laundry. No tents; small indoor pets only. Open April to late October. Transient RV park. --Claude

name: Sherk's RV Park
note: Private RV park just off Hwy 43 NW of Valleyview; ~55 sites in two loops with central pull-throughs and back-in perimeter spots, full hookups (30/50 amp, water, sewer). Store, laundry, showers, playground, walking trails. Reservable online; open seasonally ~May-Sep. --Claude

name: St. Albert Kinsmen RV Park
note: Non-profit Kinsmen Club-operated urban RV park at 47 Riel Dr, St. Albert (Edmonton area); ~93 large sites, full-service 50-amp power/water/sewer, pull-throughs, showers, dump station, WiFi. Reservable online; open ~May-Sep. --Claude

name: Entwistle RV Campground

season.note: May long weekend to about September.

note: Family-owned campground (Rainbow Beach Developments) beside the Pembina River gorge at Entwistle: 30 single sites, a tandem site and 10 group sites, with firewood included and a gated entrance.  The 2023 Parkland County wildfire left many of the single sites and trails with fewer trees; the group sites were untouched. --Claude

name: Aspen Ridge Campground
note: Private treed campground 3 km south of High Level on Hwy 35, open May-October; 41 sites - 21 full-service 30-amp with water/sewer, 10 with 15-amp+water, 10 with 15-amp - plus tent sites, hot showers, laundry and free Wi-Fi. Drive-in RV sites, reservable. --Claude

name: Beaver Glen Campground
note: Large frontcountry campground on the edge of Waskesiu townsite, Prince Albert NP: 200 back-in sites all with 15/30-amp electrical, plus 10 oTENTiks. Hot showers, flush toilets, camp kitchens, RV dump/fill station. 100% reservable via Parks Canada, mid-May to mid-Oct. Per Parks Canada Beaver Glen page. --Claude

name: Frenchman Valley Campground (West Block)
note: Frontcountry campground in the West Block of Grasslands NP near the Frenchman River: 20 electrical tent/RV sites (20/30-amp, six with 50-amp option; three pull-through, one accessible) plus 4 oTENTiks. 100% reservable via Parks Canada, mid-May to early Sept. Per Parks Canada Grasslands frontcountry page. --Claude

name: Red Deer Campground
note: 161 fully-serviced pull-through sites (water, sewer, 15/30/50-amp electric) in Prince Albert NP, walking distance to Waskesiu townsite; accommodates larger RVs. Hot showers, flush toilets. 100% reservable via Parks Canada, late May to early Sept. Per Parks Canada Red Deer page. --Claude

name: Rock Creek Campground (East Block)
note: Frontcountry campground in the East Block of Grasslands NP near Rock Creek: 24 RV-friendly electrical sites (all 50-amp) plus 8 oTENTiks. 100% reservable via Parks Canada, mid-May to early Sept. Per Parks Canada Grasslands frontcountry page. --Claude

name: Pike Lake Provincial Park
note: Large developed provincial park campground ~20 min S of Saskatoon on Pike Lake; 222 sites, all but 11 with 30-amp electrical, many pull-through, plus showers, laundry, dump station and a heated outdoor pool. Open ~May-Sept, reservable via Sask Parks (SKPP). --Claude

name: Big River Regional Park, Community Centre Campground
note: In-town campground of the Big River Regional Park (north side of the town of Big River). Community Centre Campground has 2 x 50-amp and 31 x 30-amp full-service sites, 4 non-serviced sites and 12 seasonal sites; coin showers, laundry, ball diamonds, playground. Cowan Lake town dock/boat launch nearby. Season May-Sep, reservable. --Claude

name: Carlyle Lions Campground
note: Well-treed campground in Carlyle Lions Park, west of the ball diamonds, operated by the Carlyle Lions Club for the town. 15 full-hookup sites, 30-amp, sites up to ~50 ft; modern washroom with showers and flush toilets, dump station; heated pool, playground and golf nearby. Open May-Oct, book by phone. --Claude

name: Ceylon Regional Park
note: Regional park 1 km east of Ceylon on Hwy 6, built beside the Ceylon dam/reservoir and run by the Village of Ceylon / regional park authority. 34 full-service sites (incl. ~20 seasonal) plus non-electric tenting; potable water, modern washrooms/showers, concession, outdoor pool, boat launch, fishing. Season ~May-Sep, reservable online (letscamp.ca). --Claude

name: City of Yorkton Campground
note: City of Yorkton campground on York Road (Hwy 16 W), a landscaped park minutes from downtown; 60 sites (8 pull-through, RVs to 60 ft), electric and non-electric, hot showers, city water, fenced playground and free wifi. Open mid-April to late September; call the host to reserve. --Claude

name: Davidson City Park
note: Town of Davidson city-park campground (N on Railway Ave, then E on Hamilton St), a treed setting near the swimming pool, ball diamond and golf course; 38 sites including 18 electric (15/30-amp) and 11 pull-throughs, plus a dump station and 24-hr washrooms. Open mid-May to September. --Claude

name: Dunnet Regional Park
note: Regional park (local park authority) 7 km SE of Avonlea off Hwy 339, in the Avonlea Creek valley; open ~mid-May to Sept. ~71 gravel sites incl. 66 30-amp full-service and 15-amp+water loops plus non-electric sites; heated pool, boat launch, dock, camp kitchen, laundry, modern washrooms. Reservable online (Let's Camp) or by phone. --Claude

name: Glenburn Regional Park
note: Local regional park in the North Saskatchewan River valley ~8 km S of Maymont off Hwy 376. 61 sites ranging from full-service (20/30 amp) to electric-only and non-electric; picnic table, pole BBQ, trash can per site; modern washrooms/showers, man-made spring-fed swim pond, 9-hole golf, ball diamonds. Open ~May-Sep. Reserve by phone/email; first night non-refundable deposit. --Claude

name: Shellbrook Kinsmen Campground
note: Town of Shellbrook Kinsmen campground at the Hwy 3/55 junction; 19 electrical, 4 full-service and 6 non-serviced sites, modern washrooms/showers, camp kitchen, sani-station, playground, adjacent outdoor pool. Open May long to Thanksgiving; reservable online. --Claude

name: Kipabiskau Regional Park
note: Regional park (local; Kipabiskau Regional Park Authority) on Kipabiskau Lake; 62 seasonal plus daily sites (9 15-amp, 7 30-amp, 5 non-serviced hillside, 2 lakefront 30-amp), beach showers and laundry. Open May long to Sept long; reserve by phone/email (not FCFS). --Claude

name: Lorne Calvert Campground (Wakamow Valley)
note: Municipal campground run by the Wakamow Valley Authority at 300 River Drive, on the Moose Jaw River in Wakamow Valley just S of downtown Moose Jaw. 54 open & shaded sites for tents/RVs/trailers; renovated showers, flush toilets, dump station, playground, canoe/kayak rental. Open ~May-Oct. Reservable online (Let's Camp). --Claude

name: Martins Lake Regional Park
note: Regional park (local Regional Park Authority) on Martins Lake near Leask. 59 electric (recently upgraded to 30-amp) + 9 non-serviced sites; each with picnic table & fire pit, two modern shower/washroom buildings, boat launch, swimming, golf, playground. Open ~May-Sep long weekend. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Melfort and District Regional Park
note: City of Melfort municipal campground (aka Melfort South Campground), a 16-acre well-treed park 1.6 km S of Melfort on Hwy 41 near the Hwy 3/6/41 junction. ~41 sites: 26 electric (15/30A) plus tent sites, 12 pull-throughs, dump station, showers, firewood. Reservable online; open mid-May to mid-Sep. --Claude

name: Melville Regional Park
note: ~300-acre regional park within the City of Melville with 42 campsites (15A electric, pull-throughs, water, shaded), pool, playground, ball diamonds. Day/seasonal passes plus nightly camping; reservable online (Let's Camp). Open May-Sep. Run by the Melville Regional Park Authority (local). --Claude

name: Milestone Campground
note: Small town campground operated by the Town of Milestone at the end of Railway Ave beside the pool, sport court and play park. 10 sites: 5 fully serviced with sewer, 5 unserviced; washrooms and showers. First-come, first-served (self-registration dropbox / municipal office); open June to the Sep long weekend. --Claude

name: Nipawin Regional Park
note: Regional park on the Saskatchewan River reservoir (Codette Lake) at Nipawin. 180+ serviced sites in native birch/pine/tamarack forest, level gravel pads; site types include full-service 30A (power/water/sewer) and 30A power+water, with larger 16'x85' sites for big rigs and boats. Wheelchair-accessible washrooms/showers, boat storage. Reservable online; open May to mid-Oct. Run by the Nipawin & District Regional Park Authority (local). --Claude

name: Notukeu Regional Park
note: SK regional park (local authority) adjacent to Ponteix beside Notukeu Creek, by the pool/spray park and golf course. 17 full-service 30-amp RV sites, 13 sites with water and 15-amp, plus a tenting area; showers, flush toilets, dump. Open May long weekend to end of September. FCFS on arrival; reservations by phone/email take precedence. --Claude

name: Ogema Regional Park
note: SK regional park (local authority) at the Ogema rec complex, short walk from Main Street. 44 electrical sites (mostly 30-amp) with potable water, plus group camping areas; heated swimming pool (rebuilt 2021-22), 9-hole golf. Open mid-May to Sept 15. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Oungre Memorial Regional Park
note: SK regional park (local authority) near Oungre. 75 sites, accepts big rigs; electric sites, water, showers, dump station, plus 9-hole golf, mini-golf, sports courts and an indoor aquatic centre. Open May-September (fall camping by request). Reservable. --Claude

name: Redvers Tourism Log Cabin Campground
note: Town of Redvers tourism campground on Hwy 13 beside the Red Coat Mountie statue, in the recreation complex by the pool/rec centre (local). ~56 sites, 28 full-hookup plus non-serviced; covered camp kitchen, playground, Wi-Fi. Open mid-May to early Sept. --Claude

name: Sylvan Valley Regional Park
note: Small rustic regional park in a wooded coulee near St. Victor, run by the local regional park authority. ~51 sites with 30-amp electrical, tables, grills, showers/toilets; tents welcome. Open May-Sept. --Claude

name: Bonnington Springs Campground
note: Municipal campground run by the Village of Kenaston, behind the arena near the ball diamonds and indoor pool. 22 drive-in sites with water and electric, dump station, showers and playground; open mid-May to mid-Oct. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Borden Bridge Campground
note: Leased provincial campground within the Borden Bridge Recreation Site on the bank of the North Saskatchewan River, just off Hwy 16 W. Drive-in electric+water and non-electric sites with picnic tables and firepits, shower building, on-site septic dump and river access; open mid-May to early Sep. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Nesslin Lake Campground
note: Privately-leased campground occupying the Nesslin Lake Provincial Recreation Site (provincial-forest crown land) on the west edge of Prince Albert NP, ~30 km NE of Big River. 80 non-electric + 18 serviced 30-amp sites (some sized for larger RVs) plus rental yurts, sandy beach, boat launch, canoe rental and a store; drive-in. Reservable online; open May to Sep. --Claude

name: River Valley RV Park
note: Private RV park in Langham, ~20 min west of Saskatoon, beside the Petro-Canada/Subway off Hwy 16. 48 large sites including long full-service pull-throughs; shower house, laundry, dog park, playground. Open Apr-Oct. Reservable online/by phone. --Claude

name: Val Marie Campground
note: Village of Val Marie municipal campground; well-treed, grassed drive-in sites with shade trees. ~17 sites with electric and water, sani-dump, modern accessible washrooms/showers, and a spray park; big-rig friendly. Open May-Oct. Book through the Village office. --Claude

name: Windthorst Campground
note: Village of Windthorst municipal campground on the edge of the sports grounds, just north of the community arena. 15 serviced sites: 8 full-service (power/water/sewer) and 7 with power (15/30 amp) and water; from ~$20/night. Nightly camping by self-registration at the site (first-come, first-served); washroom/shower access via the village office. Open roughly May-Sept. --Claude

name: Wasagaming Campground
note: Main frontcountry campground at Wasagaming townsite near Clear Lake, RMNP. 400+ reservable sites spanning full-hookup, electric/water, electric-only and unserviced, with both back-in and pull-through spots (many pull-throughs), plus oTENTiks/yurts; dump station on site. Open mid-May to mid-October; reservable online via Parks Canada (reservation.pc.gc.ca). --Claude

name: Bakers Narrows Provincial Park
note: Manitoba provincial park 19 km S of Flin Flon on Hwy 10, on Lake Athapapuskow. 71 electric campsites (30-amp), dump station, showers, boat launch and two swimming beaches; paved park roads suit RVs/trailers; open May-Sept. Yurts also offered. Reservable via Manitoba Parks (goingtocamp). --Claude

name: Beaver Creek Provincial Park
note: Small rustic Manitoba provincial park on the west shore of Washow Bay, Lake Winnipeg (northernmost provincial campground on the lake), ~36 km N of Riverton via PR 234. Up to 10 basic drive-in sites, self-registration (first-come, first-served), non-modern washroom, boat launch and small beach; open mid-May to Sept. --Claude

name: Camp Morton Provincial Park
note: Manitoba provincial park on the Lake Winnipeg shore 8 km N of Gimli on PR 222. 19 drive-in campsites suitable for tents/trailers/RVs, plus 14 family cabins and 6 yurts; water hookups, dump station, toilets, beach access. Campsites, cabins and yurts are all reservable through the Manitoba Parks Reservation Service (2026: May 15-Sept 19; campground open to Sept 20). --Claude

name: Clearwater Lake Provincial Park - Pioneer Bay Campground
note: Manitoba Parks campground on the NE shore of Clearwater Lake near Pioneer Bay, separate from the larger Campers Cove loop. 27 sites, 30-amp electric service, dump station and boat launch; drive-in RV-capable. Open mid-May to Labour Day; reservable online via goingtocamp. --Claude

name: Grass River Provincial Park - Iskwasum Campground
note: Manitoba Parks campground (~50 well-treed basic/non-electric sites) on Iskwasum Lake at a wide section of the Grass River, in Grass River PP near Cranberry Portage. No power/water/sewer hookups; solar gravity-fed showers, dump, boat launch/dock, swimming beach, playground. Drive-in RV access. First-come, first-served: the 2026 operating dates list Iskwasum campsites (May 15-Oct 12) with no reservation dates. --Claude

name: Grass River Provincial Park - Reed Lake Campground
note: In Grass River Provincial Park on Reed Lake, ~74 km N of The Pas off Hwy 39. 58 unserviced drive-in sites (no hookups; generator use OK), water fill and sani-dump station, boat launch, beach, fish-cleaning station, playground. First-come, first-served: the 2026 operating dates list Reed Lake campsites (May 15-Sept 7) with no reservation dates. --Claude

name: Grass River Provincial Park - Gyles Campground
note: In Grass River Provincial Park on the south shore of Simonhouse Lake, ~75 km N of The Pas. 50+ unserviced drive-in sites (no hookups), the park's accessible beach, boat launch, playground, solar showers, sani-dump. First-come, first-served: the 2026 operating dates list Gyles campsites (May 15-Sept 7) with no reservation dates. --Claude

name: Hecla/Grindstone Provincial Park - Gull Harbour Campground
note: At the north tip of Hecla Island on Lake Winnipeg. ~280 drive-in sites across six 'bay' loops; roughly 90 with 30-amp electric (a handful electric+water), back-in plus some pull-throughs, sani-dump, showers, two swim beaches (Sunset & Gull Harbour), laundry, playgrounds. Open mid-May-mid-Sept; reservable via goingtocamp. --Claude

name: Hnausa Beach Provincial Park
note: On the west shore of Lake Winnipeg, 22 km N of Gimli via PR 222. 41 drive-in sites (26 with 30-amp electric, plus basic), water spigots, sani-dump at entrance, playground, beach. Open mid-May-mid-Sept; reservable via goingtocamp. --Claude

name: Lake St. George Provincial Park
note: Quiet rustic campground in Lake St. George Provincial Park on Lake St. George, N of Hodgson via PR 224. 28 basic drive-in sites with picnic tables, fire pits, firewood; non-modern (pit) toilets, no hookups. Open mid-May-Sept. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Lundar Beach Provincial Park
note: On the east shore of Lake Manitoba, 19 km W of PTH 6 on PR 419. One campground, 33 drive-in sites (26 with 30-amp electric, 7 basic), flush toilets, showers, sani-dump, sandy beach, 3.2-km marsh trail. Open mid-May-Sept long weekend; reservable via goingtocamp. --Claude

name: Moose Lake Provincial Park
note: On Moose Lake, 32 km N of Sprague on PR 308. 96 drive-in sites (72 basic, 24 electric) including pull-through RV sites, sani-dump, showers, flush toilets, sandy beach, boat launch; grocery near the adjacent Silver Birch Resort. Some seasonal sites. Open mid-May-Sept; reservable via goingtocamp. --Claude

name: Rainbow Beach Provincial Park
note: Western provincial park on the south shore of Dauphin Lake, ~18 km east of Dauphin near Ochre River. ~72 drive-in sites incl. 28 electrical (30-amp), plus water hookups, dump station, showers, boat launch, long sandy beach, playground and walking trail; open seasonally mid-May to mid-Sept. Reservable online or by Manitoba Parks call centre. --Claude

name: Rivers Provincial Park
note: Manitoba provincial park on Lake Wahtopanah, ~1.6 km east of the town of Rivers. ~51 campsites, many with electrical service; showers, boat launch and a sandy beach. Reservable online (goingtocamp/manitobaparks), open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Stephenfield Provincial Park
note: Stephenfield Provincial Park beside the Boyne River reservoir near Carman. 134 sites (36 basic, 63 electric, 35 electric+water); 30-amp, dump station, showers, boat launch, 6 yurts. Reservable online (goingtocamp/manitobaparks), open ~mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Wekusko Falls Provincial Park
note: Manitoba Provincial Park on Wekusko Lake beside the falls on the Grass River, ~15 km south of Snow Lake. Four camping loops/bays with electric (30-amp) and non-electric sites for tents and RVs to ~35 ft; water taps, showers, dump station, boat launch and beach. Open May-Sept; reservable via goingtocamp. --Claude

name: Whitefish Lake Provincial Park
note: Manitoba Provincial Park in the Porcupine Hills boreal forest on Whitefish Lake near Birch River. About 81 non-electric (basic) sites for tents and RVs/trailers to ~30 ft; washrooms, water taps, dump station, beach and boat launch. First-come, first-served: the 2026 operating dates list Whitefish Lake campsites (May 15-Sept 20) with no reservation dates. --Claude

name: Whiteshell Provincial Park - Brereton Lake Campground
note: Small Manitoba Provincial Park campground on Brereton Lake in the Whiteshell - 28 sites (8 with 15/30-amp electric, 20 non-serviced); playground and picnic shelters; store and restaurant at the adjacent Brereton Lake Resort. Open mid-May to Sept long weekend; reservable via goingtocamp. --Claude

name: Birtle Riverside Campground and Park
note: Prairie View Municipality campground in the Birdtail River valley beside the golf course in Birtle. 30 electric/water sites + 5 full-service (water/electric/sewer) + tenting; dump station, showers, beach; open May-Sep, reservable with one-night deposit. --Claude

name: Delta Beach Campground
note: Operated by the Portage Regional Recreation Authority (PRRA, Stride Place) on the south shore of Lake Manitoba, 25 km north of Portage la Prairie on Hwy 240. Serviced ($38.50) and non-serviced ($22) sites; open May-Oct, online reservations. --Claude

name: Elkhorn Campground
note: Village of Elkhorn / RM of Wallace-Woodworth campground at the Elkhorn Agricultural Grounds off PR 256 (just off Hwy 1). ~20 sites, mix of full-service, electric, pull-through and unserviced, with dump station; open May to mid-October. Operates as a regular campground, not event-only. --Claude

name: Kelwood Centennial Park and Campground
note: Community campground at Centennial Park in Kelwood (RM of Rosedale), off Hwy 5 north of Neepawa near Riding Mountain. 22 sites with electric and electric-water 20-amp hookups, water, toilets/showers, playground and a store; open June-August. --Claude

name: MacGregor Lions Campground
note: Community campground run by the MacGregor Lions Club beside the town park and sports fields; 14 sites, 7 full-hookup plus 30-amp electric/water, showers, laundry, playground, RVs to ~45 ft, open May-Oct. Reserve by phone. --Claude

name: McCreary - Fletcher Park Campground
note: Town of McCreary's Fletcher Park Campground at the Jct of Hwy 5 & 50 in the foothills of Riding Mountain; 16 sites with 30-amp electric, showers, playground, adjacent outdoor heated pool, open May-Sept. --Claude

name: Minnedosa Campground
note: Town of Minnedosa's campground on Lake Minnedosa; ~150 sites (37 electric, 57 electric/water, 15/30-amp), sandy beach, outdoor pool, dump station, laundry, store, open May-Sept. Reserve by phone. --Claude

name: Molgat Park
note: Municipality of Ste. Rose du Lac campground on the Turtle River; ~25+ back-in and 5 pull-through sites, 30/50-amp electric/water, concrete pads, showers with heated floors, riverside trails, open May long weekend-Oct long weekend. Reserve by phone at the municipal office. --Claude

name: PortageEX Campground
note: Seasonal campground on Portage la Prairie's Island Park operated by the Portage Industrial Exhibition (agricultural society), beside the golf course and Crescent Lake; all RV sites 30-amp electric (with water), dump station, group camping, open mid-May-mid-Sept. Online reservations. Open all season, not event-only. --Claude

name: Quarry Park Campground
note: Town of Stonewall's campground in Quarry Park, a former limestone-quarry heritage park; 30-amp and full-hookup sites, big-rig sites to ~42 ft, showers, dump station, adjacent spring-fed swimming quarry and beach, walking trails, open May-Oct. Reserve online. --Claude

name: Rapid City Centennial Park Campground
note: Small town campground (Centennial Park) beside the Little Saskatchewan River reservoir below the dam, near the town pool; 8 sites with 30-amp electric and electric/water, tables, open May-Sept. First-come, first-served / arrange locally. --Claude

name: Sandy Lake Lions Club Campground
note: Sandy Lake Lions Club community campground near the Sandy Lake beach; ~52-55 sites, electric-only and electric/water, 30-amp, playground, beach and fishing within walking distance, on the Trans-Canada Trail, open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Scratching River Campground
note: Town of Morris municipal campground on the Scratching/Morris River near the Red River, ~0.4 km off PTH 75 on PTH 23 E. 24 sites, a handful with electric hookups, central water, vault toilets; playground and picnic shelter. First-come, first-served (no reservations). Open mid-May to late Oct. --Claude

name: Selkirk Park Campground
note: City of Selkirk municipal campground in Selkirk Park on the Red River. 165 sites (135 with 30-amp power), shared water, dump station; sites 15-35 ft with some pull-throughs. Reservation required via the City. Open mid-May to early Oct. --Claude

name: Welcome Stop Campground
note: Municipality of Minitonas-Bowsman free/donation campground at 315 Learners St in downtown Minitonas. 9 sites with 30-amp electric plus 2 unserviced; fire pits, picnic tables, hot showers, washrooms. First-come, first-served; open May long weekend to Sept. --Claude

name: Winkler Tourist Park
note: City of Winkler-operated municipal campground at 580 Park St, beside the Aquatic Centre in Bethel Heritage Park (walk to downtown/pool/golf). Official PLAYwinkler page: 26 drive-in sites, all with electric (15-amp sites 1-14, 30-amp sites 15-26), drinking water, dump station, washrooms/showers; max RV length ~30 ft (fits a 23-ft rig); tents allowed only on sites 1-9. Check-in at Aquatic Centre front desk. Reservable online; season ~mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Aspen Grove Campground
note: Family-run campground on the Trans-Canada Hwy 1 in the Oak Lake sandhills, 14 km E of Virden; full-service and RV sites plus tenting, heated pool, mini-golf, showers, laundry, playground, trails. Open ~May-Oct; nightly/weekly/monthly/seasonal. --Claude

name: Binscarth Park and Pool
note: Municipal (Municipality of Russell Binscarth) campground 2 km S of Binscarth; ~44 sites incl 9 full-service, 36 serviced, plus tenting areas, large heated outdoor pool, 11-hole mini-golf, playground. Open May-Oct; some seasonal, nightly available, reservable by phone. --Claude

name: Debonair Campground
note: Large family campground ~2 km from St. Malo (~200 sites): fully-serviced, partial (15/30 amp + water) and unserviced sites, private beach, 3 playgrounds, laundry, showers, dump station, trails. Open ~late Apr-mid Oct; nightly/weekly/monthly/seasonal, reservable. --Claude

name: Happyland Campground & Recreation Park
note: Municipal campground owned by the R.M. of Prairie Lakes, on the north shore of Pelican Lake at the east edge of Ninette on Hwy 23. 31 fully serviced sites (power/water/sewer) with picnic table and fire pit, plus daily/weekly/monthly stalls. Open ~May-Sept; reservable online (Let's Camp). --Claude

name: Hobbs Resort
note: Small drive-in fishing resort on the east shore of Cross Bay (Cedar Lake), ~20 min north of Grand Rapids off Hwy 6. 11 powered sites (15/30 amp + water hookup) plus 4 unserviced tent sites; also cabins and rental RV units. Boat launch, showers, fillet house. Open ~May-Sept; book direct. --Claude

name: Kerry Park Campground
note: Community campground on the north shore of Killarney Lake run by the Kinsmen Club of Killarney, off South Railway St W. 225 sites - mostly seasonal with about 25 transient - offering electric/water and full-service sites plus pull-throughs; beach, boat launch, dump station. Open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Rocky Lake Resort
note: Road-accessible lakeshore resort on the north shore of Rocky Lake near Wanless (~50 km N of The Pas); full-service and non-serviced campsites plus cabins, boat/motor rentals. Open ~mid-Feb to Nov 1; takes transient RVs, contact/reserve by phone. --Claude

name: Lower Penstemon Campground
note: USFS Sawtooth NF (Minidoka RD) in the South Hills, ~27 mi south of Hansen on Rock Creek Rd (County G3/FR515, paved-to-gravel). 6-7 single-family drive-in sites, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; ~6,600 ft. Reservable on recreation.gov (unreserved sites FCFS), open ~late May-Oct. --Claude

name: Bear Gulch Campground
note: USFS Sawtooth NF (Minidoka RD) South Hills, near Shoshone Wildlife Pond. 8 single units + 1 group, picnic tables/fire pits, vault toilets, NO drinking water, no hookups; FS notes it is suitable for trailer and tent camping, with a stock ramp/corral. First-come, first-served, free; open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Twin Lakes Campground (Albion Division)
note: USFS Sawtooth NF (Minidoka RD), Albion Division in the Albion Mts via Howell Canyon Rd (paved). Fee, non-reservation (FCFS) campground; standard nonelectric sites with fire rings/tables, vault toilets, horse corrals, NO water; ~8,200 ft, open ~July-Oct. Trailhead for Skyline Trail #513 to City of Rocks. --Claude

name: Schipper Campground
note: Sawtooth NF (Minidoka RD), South Hills along Birch Creek on Rock Creek Rd (FR 515), ~16 mi S of Twin Falls area. 5 sites, FCFS, vault toilet, no water; suited for tents with limited space for motorhomes/trailers. Season ~Apr-Oct. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Thompson Flat Campground
note: Sawtooth NF (Minidoka RD), Albion Mtns on E slope of Mt Harrison at ~8,000 ft. 25 units (21 single, 4 double; 8 reservable) plus 3 group sites; vault toilets, no water/hookups; $8/night singles. Season ~Jul-Oct. Lake Cleveland ~2 mi. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Sublett Campground
note: Sawtooth NF (Minidoka RD), ~2 mi from Sublett Reservoir; from I-84 exit 245 go ~13 mi E on Sublett Rd around the reservoir's N end. 9 units, FCFS, no fee, toilets, tables/grills, RV sites, boat ramp, no water. Season ~Jun-Nov. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Summit View Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF (Montpelier RD) campground high in the Bear River Range ~8 mi east of Hwy 30 near Georgetown, via CR-102/FR-095. 18 single-family sites plus 3 group sites at ~7,200 ft; vault toilets, drinking water, amphitheater; dirt roads and parking spurs, no hookups. Reservable online. Open ~June to early September. --Claude

name: Gravel Creek Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF, NE of Soda Springs off Wayan Loop Rd via ~4 mi maintained gravel. 12 back-in sites, gravel spurs, vault toilets, no drinking water, pack-out trash; a Campendium reviewer fit a 36-ft motorhome (~4 longer sites). First-come, first-served, $8 (free off-season), open ~late May-early Sept. --Claude

name: Calamity Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF, N end of Palisades Reservoir near the dam. ~40 nonelectric sites on 3 loops (Loop C tent-only, no trailers), picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilets, drinking water, boat ramp. Reservable online, $20; regular season late May-early Sept. --Claude

name: Curlew Creek Campground
note: Boise NF (Mountain Home RD) campground on Anderson Ranch Reservoir, ~14 mi north of Hwy 20 via Forest Hwy 61. 9 overnight drive-in sites (plus 18 day-use sites), vault toilets and potable water; no hookups. First-come, first-served. Curlew boat ramp with dock is adjacent. Good smallmouth bass and kokanee fishing. Open late May to end of September (snow dependent). --Claude

name: Lava Flow Campground (Craters of the Moon)
note: NPS campground in Craters of the Moon National Monument & Preserve off US-20/26/93 near Arco, set in the lava field just past the visitor center. 42 sites on paved pads, no hookups, no potable water reliably (haul water), flush/vault toilets in season. First-come, first-served only (not on recreation.gov). Some sites take large RVs but rigs are not recommended beyond site 15 (tight turns in the far loop, RVs to ~35 ft on the front sites). Open ~May-Nov depending on snow. --Claude

name: Abbot Campground
note: Sawtooth NF (Fairfield RD) campground on the South Fork Boise River ~2.3 mi east of Featherville; 11 sites (7 single/2 double), vault toilets, no potable water, fire rings/picnic tables. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Access via gravel FR-227. UTVs/ATVs allowed in/out of the campground only. Season mid-May-Oct. --Claude

name: Chaparral Campground
note: Sawtooth NF (Fairfield RD) campground on the South Fork Boise River ~3 mi east of Featherville on FR-227 (gravel); ~15 RV/tent sites incl pull-throughs (7 single/3 double), vault toilets, no potable water (nearest water 9 mi E near Baumgartner). First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Fees $6 single/$12 double, mid-May-Oct. --Claude

name: Bird Creek Campground
note: Small Sawtooth NF (Fairfield RD) campground on the South Fork Boise River east of Featherville; 5 sites (4 single/1 double) usable by RVs or tents on a narrow strip between gravel FR-227 and the river, vault toilet, no potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Fees $6 single/$12 double, May-Oct. --Claude

name: Canyon Transfer Camp
note: Sawtooth NF (Fairfield RD) campground on Big Smoky Creek ~25 mi N of Fairfield via gravel FR-094/227/085; 7 single + 3 group sites in an open meadow, potable water (hand pump), vault toilets, plus horse corrals/stock loading station (open to all campers, not horse-only). First-come, first-served. Fees $6 single/$12 double, May-Oct. Big Smoky Trail #072 to Skillern Hot Springs starts at the north end. --Claude

name: Star Hope Campground
note: Salmon-Challis NF (Lost River RD), wooded setting along Star Hope Creek in the Copper Basin Loop area; reached via Trail Creek Rd + Copper Basin Rd/Loop (long maintained gravel). 21 units, 2 hand pumps (summer water), 3 vault toilets. Open Memorial Day weekend to end of Sep. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Big Bayhorse Campground
note: Salmon-Challis NF at Big Bayhorse Lake, ~13 mi SW of Challis via Hwy 75 then FR 051 (narrow, steep dirt road -- caution advised; best fit under ~32 ft). High-mountain lake ~8,600 ft; vault toilets, non-motorized boat launch/docks, no drinking water. Opens ~July 1. First-come, first-served, free. --Claude

name: Fir Creek Campground
note: Small first-come, first-served USFS campground in Bear Valley (Boise NF, Lowman RD) on Elk Creek at ~6,350 ft; vault toilet, no potable water; fee-free, open mid-June-Sept. Access via gravel Bear Valley Rd (FS 579). Temporarily closed for hazard-tree removal per FS (2026). --Claude

name: Big Eightmile Campground/Trailhead
note: Salmon-Challis NF (Leadore RD), ~14 mi W of Leadore on Big Eightmile Creek at 7,549 ft via Lee Creek Rd + FR-096 (gravel). 10 sites with tables/fire rings and vault restroom; max RV length 30 ft. Open July-Sept. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Penn Basin Campground
note: Boise NF (Cascade RD), Warm Lake/Landmark area. 6 primitive drive-in sites in a mountain meadow beside Johnson Creek (tributary of the South Fork Salmon), reached via FH 22 / FSR 579 / FSR 413 (narrow, may be rough but passable by most vehicles). Picnic table, fire ring and grill per site; vault toilets, NO potable water, no hookups; open early June-late Sept. First-come, first-served. High elevation (~6,600-7,000 ft). --Claude

name: Warm Lake Campground
note: Boise NF (Cascade RD), near the eastern shore of Warm Lake at ~5,300 ft off FSR 579. 7 standard nonelectric drive-in sites, reservable on recreation.gov; vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; open mid-May-mid-Sept. Individual site RV limits run ~30-35 ft. FS notes the lake is not visible from the campground (swim beach ~1/4 mi away at Warm Lake Lodge). --Claude

name: South Fork Salmon River Campground
note: Boise NF (Cascade RD), near Warm Lake off FSR 474 with Chipmunk Creek running alongside. 11 drive-in sites in a scenic old-growth ponderosa pine forest (partial shade); potable water on-site, vault toilets, no hookups; open mid-May-mid-Sept. Appears first-come, first-served (not listed on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Trout Creek Campground
note: 5 primitive sites near Landmark in dense pine, Boise NF Cascade RD; fire rings/grills/tables and vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups; accessed by most vehicles on narrow, sometimes rough forest roads (FSR 579/413) near Johnson Creek; early June-late Sept; First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Lafferty Campground
note: 8 sites along a small creek, Council RD (Hornet/Cuddy Mtn area), Payette NF; paved loop suited to medium RVs, vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served. Typically open mid-May through Sept/early Oct. --Claude

name: Pittsburg Campground
note: USFS (Wallowa-Whitman NF, Hells Canyon NRA) campground above the Wild & Scenic Snake River — the only RV camping on the Idaho side of Hells Canyon. 28 tent/trailer sites (many accommodate large RVs) with paved loop and camp spurs, vault toilets, seasonal drinking water (Apr-Oct); $15/night, first-come, first-served. Access via Deer Creek Rd/FR 493 from US-95, a steep, narrow, winding 17.5-mi gravel road — use caution with trailers. --Claude

name: Selway Falls Campground
note: USFS (Moose Creek RD, Nez Perce-Clearwater NF), 7 sites along Meadow Creek near its confluence with the Selway River at Selway Falls; vault toilet, no potable water; accommodates RVs under 30 ft. First-come, first-served, $8/night self-pay (May-Oct); access via gravel FR 223 (FS rates access difficult). NOTE: closed for the 2026 season due to fire impacts. --Claude

name: Jerry Johnson Campground
note: Nez Perce-Clearwater NF campground along US-12 (~53 mi east of Lowell) across from the Wild & Scenic Lochsa River, near the popular Jerry Johnson Hot Springs trailhead; 20 first-come, first-served sites, $14/night, tables, fire rings, vault toilets, potable water currently unavailable. Season ~June-October. --Claude

name: Noe Creek Campground
note: Small USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, North Fork RD) campground on FSR 250 ~41 mi east of Pierce, in fir/larch with views of the North Fork Clearwater River. 6 units, small nightly fee, first-come first-served; outhouse, no potable water. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Washington Creek Campground
note: USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, North Fork RD) riverside campground on the banks of the North Fork Clearwater River, reached by a bridge off FSR 250. 23 sites (incl 1 group) plus host; gravel pads, picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, potable water spigots. First-come first-served, ~$10/night, open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Kelly Forks Campground
note: USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF, North Fork RD) campground at the confluence of Kelly Creek and the North Fork Clearwater River, on FSR 250. 14 sites plus a group area and host; RV access (no hookups), pit toilets, potable water, fire rings, tables. First-come first-served, ~$14/night, open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Hidden Creek Campground
note: USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) campground in old-growth cedar adjacent to the North Fork Clearwater River (~3,400 ft). 13 drive-in sites plus one group tent pad, vault toilets, well-spaced sites, no garbage service (pack-out). Water shut off after 9/30. First-come, first-served. Open ~late May to mid-Oct. RV Life 0*/$ unrated (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Aquarius Campground
note: USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) campground on the bank of the North Fork Clearwater River (~1,700 ft). 9 developed drive-in sites plus 2 Purple Beach group sites; swimming, fly fishing, tubing, OHV. Vault toilets, water shut off after 9/30. First-come, first-served; $10/night. Open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. RV Life 0*/$ unrated (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Dog Creek Campground (North Fork Clearwater)
note: USFS (Nez Perce-Clearwater NF) small primitive campground on the North Fork Clearwater River corridor, ~2 mi north of Aquarius. Gravel access, vault toilets, no hookups or potable water; direct river access. Drive-in but small/primitive sites. First-come, first-served. Open ~mid-May to late Sept. RV Life 0*/$ unrated (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Kelly Island Campground
note: BLM campground in a cottonwood gallery forest on the South Fork Snake River, ~23 mi NE of Idaho Falls (gravel access road off Kelly Canyon rd). 14 single sites ($10) + doubles, pull-throughs, central water spigot, vault toilets, day-use area, boat access; no hookups; pets not permitted; seasonal gate (May-Sep). Singles FCFS; 1 group site (fits ~4 large RVs) reservable online. --Claude

name: Stoddard Creek Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF (Dubois RD), 1 mi off I-15 ~17 mi N of Dubois. 21 single sites + 1 group site in Douglas fir/aspen; no hookups, vault toilets, solar-powered drinking water (arrive with water in your tanks), Stoddard Creek runs below the sites. Reservable online, open ~late May-late Sept. --Claude

name: Big Sage Campground - Lake Cascade State Park
note: Lake Cascade State Park, eastern shore. 17 sites (1 ADA), no hookups; sandy beach and lake access, boat ramp a short drive away. Reservable through Idaho State Parks, open ~May-mid Sept. --Claude

name: Lake Cascade State Park - Sugarloaf Campground
note: Lake Cascade State Park, on Sugarloaf Point on the eastern shore. 45 sites (2 ADA), no hookups; boat ramp and sandy-beach/lake access. Reservable through Idaho State Parks, open ~May-mid Sept. --Claude

name: Lake Cascade State Park - Ridgeview Campground
note: Lake Cascade State Park, near the dam just outside Cascade. One of the park's serviced loops with power at every site plus showers and clean restrooms. Reservable through Idaho State Parks, open ~May-mid Sept. --Claude

name: Lake Cascade State Park - Crown Point Campground
note: Lake Cascade State Park, Crown Point on the eastern shore just outside Cascade. 25 sites (3 ADA), no hookups; beach and lake access. Reservable through Idaho State Parks, open ~May-mid Sept. --Claude

name: Spring Gulch Campground
note: BLM Challis Field Office campground on the Upper Salmon River, ~10 mi north of Challis on US-93. 10 drive-in sites, potable water, vault toilets, river/fishing access; no hookups. First-come, first-served, open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Smokey Cubs Recreation Site (BLM)
note: BLM Salmon Field Office campground ~4 mi NE of Leadore off SH-29 toward Bannock Pass, at the base of the Beaverhead Mtns. 8 sites suited to RVs/trailers and tents, water, vault toilets; free, first-come, first-served, open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Heyburn Riverside RV Park
note: City of Heyburn RV park on the Snake River (7th St), in the Magic Valley. 29 full-service sites: 13 back-in, 9 pull-through, 7 pull-in; restrooms/showers, adjacent arboretum and paved riverfront trail, boat slips, good bass fishing. Reserve by phone with the camp host (Mar-Aug), pay via Access Idaho. Closed Dec 1-Mar 1. --Claude

name: Jerome County Fairgrounds
note: Jerome County fairgrounds; non-fair RV camping on paved pull-through lots with 30-amp electric + water, ~$20/night, roughly mid-April to mid-Oct; no on-site restrooms (store/gas a block away). Self-pay at the office, no reservations; spaces limited during fair/events. --Claude

name: Garfield Bay Campground
note: Bonner County park on Garfield Bay of Lake Pend Oreille, across the road from a public boat launch. 29 RV sites + 14 tent sites in the trees; water available at sites but NO electric/sewer and no RV water hookup; 6 vault toilets. Open weekend before Memorial Day to weekend after Labor Day; reservable online, walk-ins welcome (cash/check). Resident $22 / non-resident $30. --Claude

name: Fairway RV Park
note: Seasonal (Apr-mid-Oct) RV park operated by the Eastern Idaho State Fair in Blackfoot; 45+ water/electric drive-in sites incl large pull-thrus, dump station, restrooms/showers. First-come, first-served — honor-system lockbox pay (no reservations); recent ~$30/night. Sites fit ~30 ft; larger rigs buy two. Open all season, not event-only. --Claude

name: Cowboy Campground at Legacy Park
note: General campground on Hwy 21 just outside Idaho City offering RV, tent, and horse camping on large drive-in lots; 30 power (30/50 amp) sites added 2025-26 plus dry camping, fits any size rig; sand arena/round pens for the horse sites; seasonal Apr-early Nov, reservations recommended (call/email). --Claude

name: Riverpond Campground
note: Private drive-in RV/tent campground on the Middle Fork Payette River just outside Crouch. 24 dry RV sites with electrical hookups plus tent/campervan sites and open grass areas; community water spigot only, no dump, pit/porta toilets, no showers. On-site lily pond and guest river access. Seasonal (May-Nov), reservable online. --Claude

name: Round Valley RV Park
note: Private RV park at 211 Ramshorn Dr in north Challis. Spacious full-hookup pull-through RV sites plus tent sites; restrooms, showers, laundry, basketball court. Seasonal (Apr-Nov), reservable. Satellite shows organized planted rows of pull-throughs. --Claude

name: Andreas On The River RV Park
note: Private RV park on the Salmon River within Salmon city limits (~603 Riverfront Dr). Full hookups (30/50-amp, water, sewer), some riverfront sites with private decks; ~5-min walk to downtown Salmon. Sites accommodate large rigs; open seasonally. --Claude

name: St Joe Valley Resort
note: Riverside campground on the St. Joe River off St Joe River Rd east of St. Maries. ~30 gravel RV/tent sites, seasonal; kayaking/river-float/UTV access. Weekly rates offered but transient. --Claude

name: Navajo Lake Campground
note: Dixie NF (Cedar City RD) at Navajo Lake; 15 single + 1 double + 11 walk-in tent sites; 16 sites accept RVs/trailers 22-60 ft. Drinking water, flush and vault toilets, no hookups. Reservable via recreation.gov. Open roughly late May to late Aug. --Claude

name: Point Supreme Campground
note: NPS Cedar Breaks NM at ~10,000 ft; open ~mid-June to late Sept. 25 single-family sites; flush toilets, potable water, dump station, seasonal showers. Some sites fit larger RVs (e.g. site 15 has a 40-ft back-in driveway). Reservable on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Elkhorn Campground
note: Fishlake NF (Fremont River RD) on Thousand Lake Mountain, ~20 mi NE of Loa via U-72 then Forest Rd 206. FR-206 is a narrow, steep, single-lane dirt road for ~8 mi (passable for cautious drivers, not high-clearance-required); gravel spurs, FS lists vehicles to 70 ft. Single sites first-come first-served plus one group site; vault toilets and drinking water in season; ~9,800 ft, open Jun-Oct. --Claude

name: Mason Draw Campground
note: Small Manti-La Sal National Forest campground at ~8,300 ft off the La Sal Loop Road near the Castle Valley Overlook. 5 first-come, first-served sites, $10/night, vault toilet, fire rings, no water; June-Oct. Access is a tight, bumpy one-way gravel spur better suited to short/self-contained rigs (a 23-ft trailer has stayed). First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Twelve Mile Flat Campground
note: Manti-La Sal National Forest (Ferron/Price RD) campground near Mt. Baldy on the Wasatch Plateau at ~10,120 ft, in an open spruce/pine-rimmed meadow. Single sites (max RV ~25 ft) plus two group sites (max ~35 ft); gravel roads and spurs, vault toilets, no potable water. Reservable online (seasonal, roughly July-early Sept). RV Life 0*/$ (auto 7/2026, unrated). --Claude

name: Washington Lake Campground
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF campground on the shore of Washington Lake off the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (SR-150), elev ~10,000 ft. 43 sites (single/double family + group), concrete pads, picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, no water on site. Mix of reservable-online and first-come sites; open roughly late June-mid Sept. Canoeing/kayaking/trout fishing on the lake. --Claude

name: East Park Campground (Ashley National Forest)
note: Ashley NF, Vernal RD, on the shore of East Park Reservoir (~30 mi NW of Vernal via US-191 + FR 018/020, maintained forest road). 21 sites, vault toilets, no potable water, ~$12/night; first-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Open June-Sept. --Claude

name: Spirit Lake Campground (Ashley NF)
note: Remote high-elevation (~10,170 ft) USFS campground on Spirit Lake, Flaming Gorge RD, Ashley NF, reached via a maintained gravel road (Spirit Lake Rd/FR-001) off SR-44 — passable by a normal vehicle. 23 sites (17 combined RV/tent, 6 tent-only); a handful of the upper sites fit larger rigs (a 5th-wheel toy hauler has been seen). Vault toilets, picnic tables; no drinking water and no trash service — pack it out. First-come, first-served (not reservable). Open ~June-Sept. --Claude

name: Canyon Rim Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS Flaming Gorge NRA campground in a grassy meadow ~7,400 ft above the reservoir on Red Canyon Rd (FR-095), near Greens Lake. ~17-18 sites (about 9 tent-only); family sites with picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; open ~mid-May to mid-Sep. Reservable online with some first-come, first-served sites. --Claude

name: Red Canyon Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: Small USFS Flaming Gorge campground (8 single gravel sites) in a meadow high on the Red Canyon rim above the reservoir, by the Red Canyon Visitor Center. Vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; open ~mid-May to mid-Sep. Sites are small, un-level gravel spurs (best for rigs under ~26 ft; a 23-ft rig fits some). Mix of FCFS and reservable-online sites. --Claude

name: Hoop Lake Campground (Uinta North Slope)
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Mountain View RD) campground on the north slope of the Uintas at ~9,000 ft beside Hoop Lake, reached via gravel forest road. Standard nonelectric drive-in sites (site max vehicle length up to 42 ft), vault toilets, no potable water (come with tanks filled), no hookups. Reservable on recreation.gov. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Carmel Campground (Flaming Gorge, Sheep Creek)
note: USFS (Ashley NF, Flaming Gorge NRA) campground along Sheep Creek on the Sheep Creek Geological Loop (FSR 218) off UT-44. 15 single-family sites for tents and smaller trailers/RVs; vault toilets, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, open ~mid-May to mid-Sept. Bring water. --Claude

name: China Meadows Campground (Uinta North Slope)
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Mountain View RD) campground on the north slope of the Uintas at ~9,400 ft near China Lake and the Henrys Fork, reached via oil/gravel forest road. 9 standard nonelectric sites with gravel back-in spurs (best for shorter RVs, ~25 ft), vault toilet, no hookups. Reservable on recreation.gov. Open ~late May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Antelope Flat (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS campground (Ashley NF, Flaming Gorge NRA) on the shore of Flaming Gorge Reservoir at ~6,000 ft; 46 sites accommodating RVs/trailers roughly 20-40 ft, no hookups, flush toilets, drinking water, dump station, on-site boat ramp. Reservable online; open ~mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Lewis M. Turner Campground
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Logan Ranger District) on a wooded bench near the US-89/Beaver Mountain junction ~22 mi NE of Logan. 10 single sites, flush toilets, no hookups; per rec.gov site 5 takes RVs to 45 ft with several sites 25-30 ft. Reservable online (seasonal, roughly Jun-Sep). --Claude

name: Tony Grove Campground
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Logan Ranger District) on the mountainside above Tony Grove Lake ~19 mi E of Logan, elev ~8100 ft. 32 single + 1 double site, vault and flush toilets, no hookups; per rec.gov sites take RVs to 35 ft (tight turns favor smaller rigs). Reservable online, short season mid-July to late Sep. --Claude

name: Sunrise Campground (Bear Lake)
note: USFS Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF (Logan Ranger District), near Bear Lake Summit ~6 mi west of Garden City off US-89. 24 standard non-electric sites (2 yurts) in a wooded loop; paved roads and parking spurs, no hookups, drinking water and vault toilets. Mostly reservable online with some FCFS; roughly June-Oct. Limber Pine trailhead adjacent. First-come, first-served sites available. --Claude

name: High Creek Campground (Cache NF)
note: Small primitive USFS Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF (Logan Ranger District) campground along High Creek NE of Richmond via Forest Road 048; pavement turns to gravel and ~2 mi of gravel reaches the campground (the rough high-clearance section is past the campground toward the trailhead). ~4-5 informal drive-in sites with fire rings, no potable water, vault toilet; a 30-ft RV has stayed here per a firsthand review. Free, no fee, first-come, first-served; roughly May 15-Dec 1. --Claude

name: Kodachrome Basin State Park - Basin Campground
note: Utah State Park campground at the head of the basin ~9 mi S of Cannonville, ringed by white sandstone hills and sand pipes. Basin Campground has ~34-46 drive-in sites (paved loops/spurs), some with full hookups; drinking water, modern restrooms, hot showers, laundry, dump station; small store nearby. Open ~March-Nov. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Fremont Indian State Park - Castle Rock Campground
note: Fremont Indian SP campground in a canyon ~0.5 mi from the visitor center, off I-70. 31 single-family sites, no hookups; drinking water, flush toilets, showers; fits RVs and tents. Reservable Apr-Oct via ReserveAmerica. --Claude

name: Deer Creek State Park
note: Utah State Park on Deer Creek Reservoir near Midway. Two campgrounds (May-mid Oct): Chokecherry (40 sites, 30 full hookup) and Great Horned Owl (21 paved sites for tents/trailers/RVs up to 55 ft); flush toilets, hot showers, dump station, boat ramp. Reservable online via ReserveAmerica. --Claude

name: Antelope Island State Park - White Rock Bay Campground
note: White Rock Bay Campground on Antelope Island (Great Salt Lake), reached by the Syracuse causeway. About 20 drive-in sites with no hookups and vault/pit toilets; two equestrian sites (13-14) but otherwise a general campground suited to individuals and groups up to 16. Reservable via ReserveAmerica; typically closed Dec-Mar. Pinned to the angled pull-in sites in the valley. --Claude

name: Willard Bay State Park - South Marina Campground
note: South Marina Campground at Willard Bay State Park (Willard Bay freshwater reservoir), ~8 mi N of Ogden. Roughly 24 sites (301, 302, 304, 311-331) with full hookups plus tent sites and one group site, beside the marina; boat launch and modern restrooms; open April-October. Reservable via ReserveAmerica. Pinned to the curved loop of pull-in sites on the dike by the marina. --Claude

name: Bear Lake State Park - Rendezvous Beach
note: Utah State Parks. Rendezvous Beach on Bear Lake's south shore has four camping loops: Birch (~57 full-hookup sites), Big Creek (~46 full-hookup sites plus 1 group), Cottonwood (tent + group), and Willow (group pavilions); 30/50-amp power, water and sewer, flush toilets, showers, dump station. Reservable through ReserveAmerica. Usually open late April-late October. --Claude

name: Bear Lake State Park - South Eden Campground
note: Utah State Parks, Bear Lake Eastside. South Eden has 20 individual sites with RV power and water hookups plus 2 group sites (up to 30 people/6 vehicles); vault toilets, no sewer. Reservable through ReserveAmerica. Open approximately May-October. --Claude

name: Bear Lake State Park - North Eden (Border) Campground
note: Utah State Parks, Bear Lake Eastside (near the Idaho border; also called Border Campground). ~35 individual sites plus 1 group site, power and water hookups, vault toilets; also 120-space day-use lot with shade shelters. Reservable through ReserveAmerica. Open approximately May-October. --Claude

name: Kolob Reservoir Campground
note: PRIVATE campground (RV Life mislabels it county) on the south shore of Kolob Reservoir off Kolob Terrace Rd, ~23 mi N of Virgin; operating since 1967. Seasonal (May-Sept), adjacent to the reservoir boat ramp/dock. ~20 numbered sites; large RV/trailer parking limited to sites 1,2,4,9,16,18,19,20, some pull-throughs, max length 40 ft; vault toilets, potable water nearby; propane fires only (wood/charcoal banned). Reservable via Firefly/Hipcamp. --Claude

name: Fort Buenaventura Campground (Weber County Park)
note: Weber County park on the grounds of the historic Fort Buenaventura along the Weber River in Ogden (2450 A Ave). Mostly primitive tent/RV sites with a few electric hookups, plus 2 group sites; paved roads, dirt pads, concrete patios, tables, fire rings; 18-hole disc golf, fishing pond, trails. Best suited to smaller RVs and tent campers; first-come, first-served. Open Apr-Nov. --Claude

name: Weber Memorial Park
note: Weber County park in the South Fork Ogden River bottom below Causey Reservoir, east of Huntsville. 58 individual sites (first-come, first-served, fee paid on-site to the camp host) plus 5 group areas (A, B North, B South, C, Lodge -- reservable via Sportsites); an individual site takes one trailer + one tent; limited electricity in Areas B and C, otherwise dry camping; fire pits and picnic tables. Open first weekend of May to early October, weather permitting. First-come, first-served for individual sites. --Claude

name: North Fork Park
note: Weber County park on the east side of the Wasatch above Liberty/Eden, 2,600 acres. ~132 individual dry-camping sites across five areas (Cold Water, Cutler Flats, Loop A/B/Corrals, Middle Gate, Mustang Flats); no electric/water hookups, running water and flush toilets, fire pits, picnic tables, horse corrals. Travel trailers and pull-through sites are accommodated but the loop roads are narrow dirt, so it's best for smaller rigs; a 23-ft rig fits the drive-in sites. Group sites reservable; individual sites first-come, first-served (no reservations). Open first weekend of May to mid-October, weather permitting. --Claude

name: Duck Creek Campground
note: USFS Dixie NF campground off UT-14 ~25 mi E of Cedar City, ~2 mi W of Duck Creek Village. 70 sites (69 fit RVs 25-60 ft), flush/vault toilets, drinking water (Memorial Day-mid Sept), no hookups/showers; open ~late May-early Oct. Reservable online plus some FCFS. --Claude

name: White Bridge Campground
note: USFS Dixie NF campground on SR-143 ~12 mi SW of Panguitch along Panguitch Creek (~6 mi below Panguitch Lake), elev ~7,900 ft. 29 sites, flush/vault toilets, drinking water, dump, no hookups; single $28 / double $56; open ~mid-May to mid-Sept. Reservable online plus some FCFS. --Claude

name: Sleepy Hollow Campground
note: Rustic family-run campground at 3000 S SR-24 in Caineville, ~20 min east of Capitol Reef NP; ~20 level pull-through sites for RVs and tents, 20/30/50-amp electric + water, clean restrooms with hot showers, dump station, big cottonwoods. Seasonal May-Sep; cell dead zone, reserve by phone (paper ledger). Camper-reported rate: $40 a night for 50-amp in October 2025, $35 in May 2024 (Campendium). --Claude

name: Rocky Ridge Resort and RV
note: RV park and cabin resort at 375 W 250 N (Bullion Ave) west of Marysvale via graded dirt roads; 35 pull-through RV sites with power/water/sewer, 8 cabins, tent grass, pavilions, showers, laundry, ATV/UTV rentals, Paiute Trail access. Open ~mid-Apr to early Nov. --Claude

name: Soldier Creek Campground
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest campground at Strawberry Reservoir, ~23 mi east of Heber City on US-40 (concessionaire Utah Recreation Co.; RV Life mis-tagged commercial). 150+ single/double sites in loops A-D plus a group pavilion, paved roads, flush toilets, potable water, dump station, no hookups. Spurs 50-75 ft apart. Loops B/C/D nearest the reservoir. Seasonal (~June-Oct); reservable with some FCFS. --Claude

name: Paradise Creek Campground
note: Gifford Pinchot NF campground at the confluence of Paradise Creek and the Wind River (Mount Adams RD), ~1,660 ft. 42 back-in sites, paved spurs 20-40 ft, no hookups, hand-pump drinking water and vault toilets; premium sites sit along the Wind River. Reservable on recreation.gov, open mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Panther Creek Campground
note: Gifford Pinchot NF campground on Panther Creek off FR 65 (Mount Adams RD), ~1,010 ft. 33 back-in sites, spurs 20-40 ft, max vehicle length 25 ft, no hookups, vault toilets; premium sites adjacent to the creek. Reservable on recreation.gov, open mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Beaver Campground
note: Gifford Pinchot NF campground along the Wind River off FR 30 (Mount Adams RD), ~1,080 ft. 24 sites for tents or RVs (max vehicle length 25 ft) plus one group site, no hookups, drinking water and vault toilets; has a swingset/activity field. Reservable on recreation.gov, open mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude
